answer: Every transfer between two agents posts an escrow locked until both histories settle. An honest orchard trades with a few partners, so bonds free fast. A farm of k aliases must funnel rewards home through its own members; those k(k-1)/2 internal edges lock collateral roughly with the square of the herd, while payout grows only linearly. Each new key needs a funded edge to every sibling it pays. No safe haven for a copied sonnet of behavior: a puppet's bond frees only by the counterparty it traded with. Sparse traders stay liquid; dense collusion buries itself in its deposits.
